text: Before you can assign an owner or write a single rule, you need to know what systems actually hold LTV Global's data. This lesson builds that inventory.
Program lead Marcus Ibe runs a plain-language inventory first: for every system, what kind it is, where it runs, what data domains it holds, and what role it actually plays today.

Five systems, one row each: Atlas, the on-prem ERP holding customer, product, order, and payment data for Finance. Beacon, the cloud CRM with its own customer records for Sales. Comet, the e-commerce platform creating a third customer copy at checkout. Harbor, the warehouse system. And Summit, the Snowflake-and-Purview analytics layer that's supposed to govern everything but today governs almost nothing.

Laid out side by side, three things jump out: three independent copies of customer with no reconciliation, Summit itself being the least mature system in the inventory, and every system being well understood only inside its own department.
Next: Lesson 3 uses this inventory to identify which specific data elements at LTV Global are critical enough to govern first.
